Record date: 2129-09-19
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 09/19/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent cough with intermittent wheezing, and mild fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up visit one week after his recent hospitalization for exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and congestive heart failure (CHF). He reports that while his overall condition has stabilized, he continues to experience a persistent cough that is now dry and intermittent. The patient notes episodes of wheezing, particularly during exertion, and mentions that he feels mildly fatigued but is able to perform most of his daily activities independently.
Mr. Fairfax has been compliant with his medication regimen, including oral furosemide, prednisone, and nebulized treatments. He reports no new episodes of shortness of breath but mentions occasional feelings of tightness in his chest, particularly in the evenings. He denies any chest pain, hemoptysis, or significant weight changes since his last visit.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + mild fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + persistent cough, + intermittent wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 136/80 mmHg - Heart Rate: 80 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 20 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 91% on room air.
General: The patient appears well-nourished, alert, and in no acute distress.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Mild wheezing noted on auscultation, particularly on forced expiration; no crackles present.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) stable; persistent cough and wheezing likely secondary to airway hyperreactivity. 2. Congestive heart failure stable; no signs of fluid overload. 3. Fatigue likely related to underlying COPD and decreased physical activity.
PLAN
1. Continue oral furosemide 40 mg daily; monitor fluid status closely. 2. Taper prednisone to 20 mg daily for the next week, then discontinue. 3. Increase nebulized albuterol frequency to every 2 hours as needed for wheezing; consider adding a long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) if symptoms persist. 4. Recommend pulmonary rehabilitation to improve exercise tolerance and respiratory function. 5. Schedule a follow-up appointment in two weeks to evaluate response to treatment and reassess respiratory symptoms. 6. Reinforce education on the importance of avoiding respiratory irritants and adhering to the prescribed inhaler regimen.
Mr. Fairfax verbalized understanding of the treatment plan and expressed confidence in managing his symptoms.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with updated medication instructions and a follow-up appointment scheduled. He was advised to monitor his symptoms closely and seek medical attention if he experiences any worsening of his condition or new concerning symptoms arise.
